candidates.computation_change_reason: The table defines multiple parallel criteria families (instream waste concentration formulas, domestic supply, domestic/irrigation/livestock-wildlife criteria, acute/chronic aquatic criteria, human health criteria, and TMDL need). Which column or formula is treated as the operative requirement for a given facility, use, or parameter changes which numeric limits are selected and which monitoring parameters are in scope.

These entries label instream limits as functions of effluent concentration (Ce) and distinct domestic, chronic aquatic, and human-health derived values. Interpreting them as active calculation rules versus inert column labels changes whether applicable limits are taken from formulas, from the zero values shown beneath, or from other columns when Ca/Ce are blank.

MQL, ambient concentration (Ca), and effluent concentration (Ce) can be read as method detection/quantification thresholds, inputs to instream mixing calculations, or enforceable discharge limits. Different readings change limit applicability (A), whether monitoring at a stated quantification level was required (B), and how sub-MQL or unreported results are classified versus true missing evidence (C).

A single pollutant row simultaneously presents domestic (1 ug/l), acute aquatic (19), chronic aquatic (15), and human health (30) criteria alongside 1E+100 placeholders and instream zeros. Which value is treated as the governing enforceable limit depends on criteria-selection rules and changes exceedance determinations.

The repeated 1E+100 entries may represent no applicable numeric criterion, a non-operative placeholder, or a literal very large limit. That interpretation determines whether a numeric compliance comparison is performed at all and whether absence of an ordinary result should be treated as unbounded versus bounded missing-evidence cases.

This pollutant row lacks an MQL value where other listed pollutants include one. Whether that omission means no quantification requirement, an unstated default, or incomplete table data changes whether monitoring was required for this parameter and how to classify results that lack an ordinary numeric reported value.

candidates.computation_change_reason: The Need/TMDL column header signals whether total maximum daily load constraints may supersede or supplement the numeric criteria shown. Interpreting TMDL need as operative versus informational changes which enforceable limits are considered applicable.

Every listed pollutant shows N/A in the Need TMDL column. Whether N/A means no TMDL-based limit applies, TMDL status is unknown, or the field is non-operative changes limit selection and whether missing TMDL information leaves applicability unresolved.

Instream-waste columns are populated with zeros while Ca and Ce fields are blank for listed pollutants. Reading the zeros as enforceable zero limits, as formula outputs from absent inputs, or as non-operative placeholders changes applicable limit values and whether missing ambient/effluent data implies a resolved no-exceedance state versus unresolved evidence.

This row pairs an MQL of 50 ug/l with domestic and human-health criteria orders of magnitude lower (0.0015 and 0.002 ug/l). Whether MQL governs comparability of reported measurements versus the listed criteria changes exceedance outcomes and whether results below MQL are treated as adequate evidence or unresolved missing data.
